candidate.answerReason: The sum with the reversal is 11 times the digit sum. The only square between 11 and 198 divisible by 11 is 121, so the digits sum to 11, giving eight two-digit integers.

methods.label: Use place value and a bounded list of squares
methods.explanation:
Let \(a\) be the tens digit and \(b\) the ones digit of \(N\), so \(1\le a\le9\) and \(0\le b\le9\). Place value gives
\[
N=10a+b,
\qquad N+\text{its reversal}=11(a+b).
\]
The reversal has value \(10b+a\), even when \(b=0\).

Since \(1\le a+b\le18\), the sum lies between \(11\) and \(198\). The complete list of squares in this range is
\[
\begin{gathered}
16,25,36,49,64,81,\\
100,121,144,169,196.
\end{gathered}
\]
Only \(121\) is divisible by \(11\). Consequently
\[
11(a+b)=121,
\qquad a+b=11.
\]
For every tens digit \(a=2,3,\ldots,9\), the ones digit \(b=11-a\) is valid. These give
\[
29,38,47,56,65,74,83,92.
\]
The tens digit \(1\) would require the invalid digit \(10\), so there are no further cases. Each valid tens digit gives exactly one number, and different tens digits give different numbers. Thus the count is \(\boxed{8}\), choice \(\mathrm E\).
methods.levelReason: Place value and a short exhaustive list of integer squares give the result without formal congruences or prime-factorization machinery.

review.mathematicalCheck: Writing N=10a+b gives a reversal sum of 11(a+b), including b=0. Its range is 11 through 198. The displayed square list is exhaustive, and only 121 is divisible by 11. Thus a+b=11, yielding exactly the eight numbers with a=2 through 9.
